title: Oracle Patches Over 1,200 Vulnerabilities With October 2026 CPU
description: Oracle released its October 2026 Critical Patch Update (CPU) addressing 1,295 vulnerabilities across multiple products. Among these, 95 are rated critical severity, with Fusion Middleware receiving the most patches, including many remotely exploitable without authentication. No active exploitation in the wild has been reported. Oracle plans further monthly security updates in November and December 2026.
aiSummary: Oracle's October 2026 CPU includes fixes for 1,295 vulnerabilities spanning dozens of products. Of these, 1,209 are unique CVEs with 95 critical severity flaws, 439 high severity, and 582 medium severity. Fusion Middleware had 206 fixes, 134 of which can be exploited remotely without authentication. Other heavily patched products include E-Business Suite, Siebel CRM, Communications, PeopleSoft, JD Edwards, MySQL, and Java SE. Oracle has not reported any confirmed exploitation in the wild but acknowledges periodic exploitation attempts. The company also released a separate advisory for CVE-2026-91403 related to a Java weak-key incident. Oracle schedules monthly Critical Security Patch Updates (CSPUs) to continue addressing vulnerabilities.
aiImpact: The update addresses a large volume of vulnerabilities, including many critical and remotely exploitable flaws, particularly in Oracle Fusion Middleware and other widely used Oracle products. While no exploitation in the wild has been confirmed, the presence of remotely exploitable vulnerabilities without authentication indicates a significant risk if unpatched. The broad scope of affected products means that many Oracle customers could be impacted if they do not apply these patches promptly.
